advanced_mode.description: ESC i K <flags> — expanded mode: bit 3 (0x08) cut at end, bit 6 (0x40) 600-dpi length mode (not on this 300-dpi head), bit 0 (0x01) two-colour (QL-8x0 only). brother_ql sends 0x08.

auto_status_notification.description: ESC i ! <mode> — 0x00 turns automatic status notifications on (the printer pushes the 32-byte reply on completion, error and phase change), 0x01 turns them off.

compression_mode.description: M <mode> — 0x02 turns PackBits (TIFF) compression of raster rows on, 0x00 off. Rows keep their 67 00 <n> framing; <n> becomes the compressed length.

cut_each.description: ESC i A <n> — cut every n labels (1 = after each).

initialize.description: ESC @ — reset job state (page counter, mode flags) without touching loaded-media sensing.

invalidate.description: Invalidate — 200 bytes of 0x00 (print_geometry.invalidate_bytes) that flush any half-eaten command from the printer's buffer. First thing in a job; brother_ql sends switch_dynamic_command_mode once before it as well.

margin_amount.description: ESC i d <dots u16 LE> — feed/margin amount in dots; 35 (0x23 0x00) on continuous rolls (print_geometry.feed_margin_dots), 0 on die-cut.

print.description: FF (0x0C) — print the page and keep the job open for another (multi-page jobs).

print_information.description: ESC i z + 10 bytes: valid flags (bit 7 always set; bit 1 = media type valid, bit 2 = width valid, bit 3 = length valid, bit 6 = high-quality/priority), media type (0x0A continuous / 0x0B die-cut; features[].media[].media_type_code), media width mm, media length mm (0 = continuous), raster line count u32 LE, page number (0 on the first page, 1 after), trailing 0x00. A die-cut job on the DK-11241 roll (Brother's catalogue calls it 102x152; the media table above and brother_ql send 153): 1B 69 7A 8E 0B 66 99 <rows u32LE> 00 00.

flags.description: Valid-flag byte; 0x8E = media type + width + length valid (0x80 | 0x02 | 0x04 | 0x08); OR 0x40 for high-quality.

length_mm.description: Label length in mm for die-cut; 0 for continuous.

page.description: 0 on the first page of a job, 1 on later pages.

rows.description: Raster line count for this page, LITTLE-endian.

print_with_feeding.description: SUB (0x1A) — print the final page, feed and cut per the mode flags; ends the job.

raster_line.description: g 00 <n> <n bytes> — one print line, 1 bit per dot, MSB first, 1 = black, mirrored left-to-right before packing (print_geometry.mirror_rows), padded white to 162 bytes; n = 162 uncompressed or the PackBits length when compression_mode is on.

row.description: The row: 162 raw bytes, or its PackBits encoding.

status_information_request.description: ESC i S — request the 32-byte status reply (header 80 20 42; layout in brother_ql_raster_protocol.status_reply). The Media Width and Printer Errors sensors read this reply.

switch_dynamic_command_mode.description: ESC i a <mode> — select the command set: 00 ESC/P, 01 raster (everything here), 03 P-touch Template. Sent at the head of every raster job.

various_mode.description: ESC i M <flags> — bit 6 (0x40) auto-cut on; brother_ql sends 0x40 for auto-cut.

zero_raster_line.description: Z — one entirely white print line; saves sending 162 zero bytes.

txt_match.description: Make/model TXT — narrows the shared raw-print type to this Brother model.
Make/model TXT — narrows the shared IPP type to this Brother model.

methods.notes: This is Bluetooth CLASSIC discovery, not BLE: the name appears in a Classic inquiry, not a GATT advertisement. Recorded as a ble_scan method because the schema has no bt_classic_inquiry type; a consumer must do a Classic inquiry (or be handed the paired device) and connect over SPP — there is no BLE GATT surface.

mac_prefixes.notes: Observed on the user's unit (60:98:66:AA:BB:CC). This is the Bluetooth radio's block, not a Brother-registered OUI, so it ranks a device rather than identifying it.

device.name: Brother QL-1110NWB Label Printer
device.notes:
Wide-format (up to 4 in / 103.6 mm media) direct-thermal label printer, 300 dpi, ~110 mm/s, auto cutter, continuous prints to ~3 m. Connectivity: USB-B device, USB-A host (barcode scanners), Ethernet 10/100BASE-TX, Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n (infrastructure + Wireless Direct + WPS 2.0), and Bluetooth Classic 2.1+EDR (profiles SPP, BIP, OPP, HCRP, iAP/MFi — no BLE GATT; retailer pages claiming "Bluetooth 5.2" are aggregator noise against Brother's own spec sheet). AirPrint/MFi certified, so IPP on 631 and Bonjour advertisement are also present.
COMMAND LANGUAGES: the printer accepts three command sets, selected with ESC i a — 00h ESC/P (text-mode printing), 01h raster graphics mode (the one everything below documents), 03h P-touch Template mode (print stored templates with merged data from a host; commands are ^-prefixed per Brother's P-touch Template Command Reference). Brother publishes a Raster Command Reference for the QL series, so the raster language is a vendor-documented API, not a recovered one; brother_ql is the reference open implementation and the source of the per-model geometry here.
PRINT TRANSPORTS: the same raster byte stream goes over TCP RAW port 9100 (primary; also reachable as _pdl-datastream._tcp via Bonjour), LPR/LPD port 515, FTP port 21 (drop a raster file), Bluetooth Classic SPP, or USB. A raster job is: switch-to-raster-mode → 200×0x00 invalidate → ESC @ → media/quality → cut/margin settings → raster rows → 0x1A. See the brother_ql_raster_protocol block for the byte-level tables.
STATUS: ESC i S (1B 69 53) requests a 32-byte status reply (header 80 20 42) carrying error bitmasks, loaded-media type/width/length, and job phase; ESC i ! (1B 69 21) toggles automatic status notifications. On the network, Brother also exposes printer status over SNMP (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.2435.3.3.9.1.6.1.0 per Brother's developer FAQ) and a web admin page on port 80.
CONFIDENCE: high for the command set (vendor-documented + implemented by brother_ql against real QL hardware), lower only where noted (RFCOMM channel, Wireless Direct defaults).

openness.notes: Brother's command references are the authoritative text; brother_ql (pklaus/brother_ql) is the reference open implementation, tested against real QL-series hardware and the source of the per-model geometry (162 bytes/row, invalidate count, min/max length) used here. A consumer wanting a working client should use brother_ql directly — this spec exists to document the protocol, not to compete with it.

factory_reset.effect: Three scopes, chosen by Cutter-press count: ×2 resets network settings; ×4 resets transferred data (templates/databases) and device settings; ×6 resets everything to factory settings. Public user-manual procedure.

steps.action: Press and hold Power and Cutter for about one second.
steps.expect: Status LED lights orange, Wi-Fi LED flashes green.

steps.action: While still holding Power, press Cutter 2× (network reset), 4× (data + device settings) or 6× (full factory reset).

steps.expect: LEDs flash, then the printer restarts with the chosen scope cleared.

methods.description: WPS or Wireless Direct from the printer's own buttons; USB + Printer Setting Tool; or DHCP on Ethernet. Details in docs/devices/brother-ql-1110nwb.md.
methods.name: Network join from the printer's own buttons

steps.action: Join the printer to the LAN (WPS / Wireless Direct / USB tool / Ethernet).
steps.expect: The printer answers mDNS _pdl-datastream._tcp and accepts TCP 9100.

methods.description: Bluetooth Classic path (recorded under ble_direct for want of a bt_classic setup type): press the printer's Bluetooth button, pair with QL-1110NWB<serial-suffix> from the host, then open an SPP connection (standard SPP UUID 00001101) and send the same raster byte stream.
methods.name: Bluetooth Classic pairing with the host OS

steps.action: Press the Bluetooth button on the printer.
steps.expect: Bluetooth LED lights; printer discoverable as QL-1110NWB0000-style name.

steps.action: Pair from the host and open an RFCOMM/SPP connection.
steps.expect: Byte stream accepted exactly as on TCP 9100.

setup.notes: Printing itself needs no account and no cloud — any transport that carries the byte stream works. Setup is only about getting the printer onto the LAN or paired. Options (per Brother's user manual): WPS (WPS button + router WPS), Wireless Direct (the printer hosts its own AP, SSID of the form DIRECT-xxxxx_QL-1110NWB), USB configuration with Brother's Printer Setting Tool, or Ethernet (DHCP) for the wired path. Bluetooth Classic pairing is enabled with the Bluetooth button; the printer then advertises as QL-1110NWB<serial-suffix> and prints over SPP. None of these flows has been replayed by this project.

rejoin.notes: Re-running WPS or the USB Printer Setting Tool re-points the printer at a new network without a reset; the 2× Cutter network reset is the clean fallback.

testing.notes: The printer itself is physically present in the project's test environment (observed advertising on Bluetooth Classic as "QL-1110NWB0000", MAC 60:98:66:AA:BB:CC), but no print job or status request from this document has been driven against it. Every protocol fact here comes from Brother's own published command references and the hardware-tested open implementation brother_ql.

variants.notes: The networked model this spec is written for: 300 dpi, 162 bytes/row (1296-dot head), 200 invalidate bytes, media 12–103.6 mm (DK die-cut and continuous rolls), monochrome.
USB-only sibling: same engine and raster language (same 162 bytes/row geometry in brother_ql), no network or Bluetooth — USB transport only.
Near-identical successor; brother_ql assigns it the same model parameters as the QL-1110NWB.

local_access.summary: Fully local as shipped: raster printing over TCP 9100 / LPR / FTP / SPP / USB with no account and no cloud anywhere in the path.

geometry.note: MOVED: the numbers (dpi, bytes_per_row, head_dots, invalidate_bytes, min/max_length_dots, additional_offset_right_dots, feed margin) are now declared under features[image_upload].print_geometry, which is authoritative. Every raster row is exactly 162 bytes wide; content narrower than the head is padded white on the right (the last 44 dots of the head do not print — right-side dead zone). Continuous media needs ESC i z media length = 0 and lets the raster row count set the label length (301–35434 dots, i.e. ~25.5 mm–3 m).

job_structure: 1B 69 61 01   switch to raster mode (also emitted once before the invalidate run)
00 × 200      invalidate — clears any half-eaten command in the buffer
1B 69 7A …    print information / media and quality (see commands.print_information)
1B 69 4B 08   expanded mode: bit 3 = cut at end (bit 0 two-color and bit 6 600-dpi do NOT apply to this 300-dpi monochrome head)
1B 69 64 23 00  margin/feed amount, u16 LE dots (35 typical)
4D 02          (optional) enable PackBits compression of raster rows
raster rows   one opcode per print line (see raster_rows)
1A             print final page (0C prints an intermediate page in multi-page jobs)

media.note: MOVED: the roll table (width/length in mm, total and printable dots, right offset, feed margin, media-type code) is now declared under features[image_upload].media, which is authoritative and carries every DK roll brother_ql lists for this model rather than the eleven this block used to. ESC i z takes the media width/length in mm.

raster_rows.compression_toggle: 4D <mode>            (02 = on, 00 = off; rows keep the 67 00 framing but carry PackBits data)
raster_rows.encoding: 1 bit per pixel, MSB first, 1 = black. The image is mirrored left-to-right before packing (the head maps bit 7 of byte 0 to the RIGHT edge), padded to 162 bytes with white on the right.
raster_rows.two_color_row: 77 <01|02> <n> <n bytes>  (QL-800-series red layer; not applicable here)

fields.bits: 0 no media, 1 end of media (die-cut), 2 cutter jam, 4 main unit in use, 5 printer off, 7 fan failure
fields.name: error_information_1

fields.bits: 0 replace media, 1 expansion buffer full, 2 communication error, 4 cover open during print, 6 media cannot be fed, 7 system error
fields.name: error_information_2
media_type
fields.values: 0x00 none, 0x0A continuous length tape, 0x0B die-cut labels

fields.name: status_type
fields.values: 0x00 reply to status request, 0x01 printing completed, 0x02 error occurred, 0x05 notification, 0x06 phase change

status_reply.notes: A completed job shows up as a status_type 0x01 followed by a phase change to "waiting to receive"; a consumer polling for job completion watches for that pair. ESC i ! +1 enables/disables the printer pushing these replies unsolicited.

brother_ql_raster_protocol.transport: Raw byte stream, identical on every carriage: TCP 9100 (RAW/AppSocket), LPR/LPD 515, FTP 21 (file drop), Bluetooth Classic SPP, or USB bulk. No framing, no authentication; the printer consumes the stream as-is.

remaining_unknowns: The top-level `commands` schema has no raw-byte-stream transport, so the raster opcodes above are documentary (`payload_hex`, an undeclared key) rather than executable by a generic renderer; a `tcp-raw`/`byte-stream` transport arm with `value`/`template` is the missing piece.

Narrow-media centring (right_margin_dots on the smallest rolls) is transcribed from brother_ql and has not been driven on this unit; the mobile handler's caveat that it is a calibration question stands.
No job from this document has been printed by this project (device.testing is untested); every opcode is `reported` from Brother's reference and brother_ql.
